hero.title: Lineage Tracer
hero.subtitle: Trace a column from the dbt model that builds it to the Power BI visual that renders it — through Power Query renames, measures and calculation groups.

banners.name: section-inputs
banners.title: The four files it needs
banners.body: manifest.json, catalog.json, a mapping file and the PBIP project folder. All four are required — Build lineage stays disabled until every slot is filled.

banners.name: section-mapping
banners.title: The mapping file
banners.body: The one input no parsing can replace. Every declared link between a dbt column and a semantic model column lives here — renames, native SQL sources, an intervening view. Required, always.

banners.name: section-lineage
banners.title: The lineage canvas
banners.body: One left-to-right DAG in swimlanes, from dbt sources through to Power BI visuals. Table nodes expand to their columns; selecting a column dims everything except its path.

banners.name: section-impact
banners.title: Impact analysis
banners.body: Blast radius is exact graph traversal and always shown with raw counts. A BROKEN chip appears only where the artifacts prove it. There is no heuristic CRITICAL.

banners.name: section-layout
banners.title: Page layout
banners.body: The affected visuals as wireframe boxes, in place on the report pages they live on — a name tells you what to look for, a position tells you where to look.

banners.name: section-diagnostics
banners.title: Diagnostics
banners.body: Eleven sections of everything that did not link, graded error, warning or info, each row linking back into the graph. This is the worklist your mapping rows come from.

banners.name: section-reference
banners.title: Gotchas, privacy and licences
banners.body: Everything below is reference — read it when you need it. What will bite you, what the tool deliberately does not protect against, and who owns the vendored code.

banners.name: section-start
banners.title: Where to start
banners.body: Four ways in, depending on what you came for — a graph out of it today, a tour of what it renders, why something did not link, or how it is built.

banners.name: section-problem
banners.title: The gap between two good tools
banners.body: dbt and Power BI each have good lineage tools, and both stop at the warehouse boundary — the one place a column's story crosses systems. Today that gap is crossed by hand.

banners.name: section-who
banners.title: Who this is for
banners.body: Analytics engineers, BI developers, data platform leads and reviewers — four people who ask the same question from four different ends of the chain.

banners.name: section-wired
banners.title: How it is wired
banners.body: What parses what, where it runs, and which links are declared by you versus derived by the tool.

banners.name: section-export
banners.title: One file you can email
banners.body: The same graph, canvas and panels with the data baked in. No server and no sidecar assets — double-click it and it opens.

banners.name: section-why
banners.title: Why this tool
banners.body: What it does that a dbt lineage graph and a Power BI lineage view cannot, side by side.

banners.name: section-faq
banners.title: Questions people ask first
banners.body: What it needs, what it does with it, what it cannot do, and what happens to your files.

cta.name: cta
cta.label: Open Lineage Tracer
cta.sublabel: runs in your browser  ·  no account  ·  nothing is uploaded

strips.name: strip-why
strips.label: No setup, nothing leaves the tab, the formats you already have

cards.title: No setup, no waiting
cards.body: Open the page, drop in your files, press Build lineage. Nothing to install, nothing to provision, nothing to wait for.

cards.title: Nothing leaves the tab
cards.body: No API, no upload path, no telemetry, no account, no stored state. Your files are read where they already are.

cards.title: The formats you already have
cards.body: dbt manifest.json and catalog.json, a mapping file as .csv, and your PBIP project folder.
